narracao: A board of five put the harbor in San Pedro, four votes to one, and not at the railroad's pier. And a city nineteen miles from the harbor towns drew a strip half a mile wide to touch them, then voted itself onto the coast. The strip was never a road to the sea. It was the way to a deep-water harbor that didn't exist yet. The strip is still on the map. So is the water.
